heading: Publication

calibration.note: Same one-paper profile (14 proofs of arXiv 0708.2185); no new measurement was made for this problem. The rules are restated for a two-case proof with one auxiliary construction and one cited principle.

length_basis_rhgrh100.note: The 120/168 limits came from one paper whose own median proof is about 48 words; against this corpus they sit between the 41st and 53rd percentile, so they are kept.

sentence_sample_rhgrh100.sample: 60 proofs of 40-400 words, one per paper, from mark7rhgrh100-20260928; two annotators (codex-18, zai-2), same instrument as the one-paper profile
sentence_sample_rhgrh100.reading: PR1 holds on 60 papers: commentary-only sentences are about 1 percent of proof words or less for both annotators, and most of zai-2's in-flight labels are sentence fragments. PR3 holds: separate side-condition sentences are rare. The one-paper lemma-application share (32-42) is high for this corpus (about 25, wide spread). Section lead is not reliably measured: the annotators disagree on whether setup sentences count (per-proof correlation 0.01). About one proof in twelve opens with a one-sentence statement of method (by induction; following a cited argument), which PR2 as worded would forbid; no pilot telling uses one.

rules.rule: No sentence may be commentary only (placement inflight or leaf-section). A reason for a step may appear only as a clause of the sentence that takes the step.
No restatement of the claim before the derivation; the proof opens with its first step.

The boundary form of the maximum modulus principle is invoked in one sentence that says what it consumes (a polynomial, and a point of the closed unit disk) and what it returns. Compactness of the disk, which makes the supremum finite, is a clause and not a separate check.
At most 168 words; aim for 120 or fewer.
Every mandatory node of the content plan is realized or merged with an honest quote; every dependency between nodes in the alignment is still visible in the prose.
rules.from: programme gate for P3 and P4

reflection-strategy.reason: Answered as a purpose clause inside the sentence that introduces the reflected polynomial; no separate sentence.

maximum-modulus-applicability.reason: PR3 requires the invoking sentence to say what the principle consumes, which is this question's answer.

circle-to-disk-transfer.reason: How a boundary bound reaches the interior is the content of the cited principle; a paper cites it and does not unfold it.

unit-disk-supremum-bound.reason: The defining bound of a supremum is used without justification beyond the compactness clause.

note: Question decisions differ from the expert-reference profile in one place: the applicability question is anticipated here because PR3 makes the citing sentence name its hypotheses. Lengths (PR4) and the accounting of all nine nodes (PR5) also differ.
